cross_axis_notes.text: Single-store, single-selling-entity checkout (one order, one storefront, one legal seller). A1 only supplies the storefront binding on sale routes (A1-13); order splitting and the legal-entity snapshot on the order belong to checkout.

Local pricing without automatic FX and the three-decimal currencies KWD, BHD, OMR. StorefrontContext.currency is read by no price code (PR 47 body, price-stock map README); the currency seam is separate work.

Order acceptance stays independent of a country merely existing in the system. GCC-11 legal readiness (PRs 38, 39, 42, 43, 49) decides sellable; A1-02 only needs active to stay separate from sellable.
Purchase from a non-active country depends on the delivery address eligibility. StorefrontSellingGate checks only the storefront's legal readiness, never the delivery address.

SEO, canonical URLs, hreflang, redirects and sitemaps per market. DECISIONS says SEO must be market-scoped; the GCC tree adds no SEO, sitemap or canonical-URL code (checked by file names and by the added lines of git diff main..PR 83), and hreflang today follows installed languages, not markets.

App Links and Deep Links with market paths. Not assessed in A1; the GCC tree changes no deep-link route or association file (its only deep_link is a navigation key in the platform-admin alert payload).
Theme caches: PR 37 scopes the StorefrontThemeRenderer and ThemeDelivery keys per market and forgets every market's copy on publish. Per-market theme drafts and publishing are the theme unit's.

Cart and guest cart per storefront (PR 48 StorefrontCartScope, moveGuestCartToCustomer) and one customer identity across markets (GCC-13). A1 lists them only as examples of context in sessions and sign-in (A1-12).

Per-store pause (GCC-12 in DECISIONS: browse-only, maintenance page, redirect to default) decides when a default or a market is operational (A1-03). No pause exists in code (searched app, config, routes, database).

Per-country legal entity with its own gateways, bank accounts, invoices and taxes, and per-country catalogue, inventory, themes and integrations. A1 only asks that the entity concept exists apart from the storefront (A1-09); accounts and ledgers belong to payments and finance.

Staff country scopes (GCC-14c, PRs 74, 77, 82) and the platform admin API with its explicit market parameter (GCC-20, PRs 71, 79, 80, 84) are separate context mechanisms that read the same registry and the same product column.
Notification content, templates and per-market senders (the market-scoping rule itself is A1-17).
Fulfillment source per product per country, inventory locations, pools and reservations (the market-scoping rule itself is A1-18).

cross_axis_notes.text: Stock numbers, reservations, inventory pools and the fulfilment source per product per store are independent per country. B owns only that price and stock sit on the country's own product row; provider connections have no country yet (B-05 serves the default storefront until they do).

One store and one selling company per checkout, and no cart mixing sellers of different countries. B supplies the country of every product (B-01); the cart guard (#48) and the sale gate (#49) are checkout work.

Orders keep an immutable snapshot of company, currency, tax, prices, address and fulfilment source, and refunds use the original currency. Orders record no country or currency today (price-stock map gaps 6 to 10), which blocks B-03 for invoices, e-mails and exports.
Compatibility of the single-store checkout with multi-vendor orders and sub-orders. Seller products are SA-only today (B-09).

Coupon rules (minimum purchase, amounts and currency per store, limits, eligible items, redemption) and central-campaign market selection (GCC-17) are coupon-rule work; B-16 covers only what is displayed per storefront.
Theme: which sections, banners and categories a storefront's theme shows, and the theme caches per storefront (#37), belong to the theme unit; B-15 covers banner data only.

Staff country scopes for orders, POS, refunds, reports, vendors, promotions and storefront content (slices 2 to 6: #77 and #82, then open) belong to the staff-permissions unit; B-08 covers only the product screens (#74).
Category-level tax class, shipping cost per seller and category, governance and commission rows are single global rows; a per-country tax or shipping policy belongs to the tax and shipping units.
purchase_price (cost) is still in customer-facing product JSON; stripping it is an open owner decision (price-stock map finding 3).
The storefront chooser, the X-Storefront header and the app caches of the customer and seller apps (lavkooapp #1 to #7, lavkooappseller #1 and #2) are store-context and mobile work; B consumes them.

Not every Blade view or theme file was read for hard-coded country, currency or price display; only the files named in the evidence were. Whether the web filter sidebars hide brands or categories with zero products is UNVERIFIED.

cross_axis_notes.text: GCC-19 default storefront: Saudi at launch, changeable by the admin, and the chosen default must be valid and operational. StorefrontResolver refuses an inactive default; choosing and changing it in the admin is six-country base work.

Paths /sa to /om, old links, SEO and canonical URLs, App Links and Deep Links. No storefront chooser exists on the website or in the apps (runbook known limits); D1-17 only pins how a request resolves.

IP-based country inference ranking below the manual choice: no inference code exists in the backend (the monitoring panel says no GeoIP database is installed). D1-17 pins choice, header, path, default only.

Models for warehouse, fulfillment provider account, sales-channel account and customer identity are not part of D1-04, which keeps only the order-side keys. One login across countries (GCC-13) is identity work.

Gateway and bank accounts per legal entity, the merchant account on the payment attempt, gateway refunds (the MyFatoorah refund row already carries currency) and the reconcile check of amount and currency, which needs the order currency of D1-06.
Per-country product price entry, copy-to-country tool, SKU and barcode uniqueness per country (#64, #72, #76). D1-05 only consumes the price at checkout.
Provider accounts and warehouses per country, stock pools and reservations, country-specific providers. D1-09 only freezes the chosen provider on the order line.
Shipping eligibility rules (product by destination, provider coverage, regulated pharmacy goods checked apart from courier coverage). D1-17 owns only the order-time gate that will call them.

Wallet and loyalty at checkout and refund: whole-cent USD debit in every store currency (#36), refused-debit handling (#12), POS wallet atomicity (#13, #35), wallet credit per entity and currency. Order totals are assumed USD in #36.

Staff country scopes on orders, POS and refunds (#77, #82, GCC-14) derive an order's country from its lines because orders carry none; once D1-01 stamps it they should read the stamp, with the line rule as fallback.

Legal text approval, the recorder of explicit acceptances (#43, not called by checkout) and the per-store pause modes of GCC-12 (browse-only, maintenance page, redirect). D1-16 owns only the refusal at the sale routes.
Coupon use limits, first-order and referral counts are per customer across all orders (E09-F14); per-store limits, amounts and currency (GCC-17) are coupon work. Coupon minimum tests are #2, #4, #5.
Odoo posting, the vendor ledger and the single platform wallet (admin_id 1) per legal entity need the entity key from D1-03 before they can be split.

Customer app takes its currency from the global config and sends current_currency_code at checkout; per-storefront currency and the browse-only notice on a device are app work. The seller app must send Idempotency-Key for the POS sale of #35.

coverage_gaps: Read-only assessment: no test, build or CI log was run or read. CI facts come from ci-table.md and ci/*.json (job-level conclusions, latest attempt, 2026-11-18). That a named test ran inside a green job is inferred from the path lists in .github/workflows/ci.yml of the PR 83 and PR 18 heads, not from job logs.

No combined security and GCC tree exists. File overlaps between the two sets and the p0 PRs were computed from git diff --name-only against main, not from a merge, so real textual conflicts beyond the five known files are untested.

Production values are unavailable: currency_model, system_default_currency, decimal_point_settings, the tax set-up, whether real vendors other than the in-house shop exist, and the real schema (installation/backup/database.sql is not in the repository). All are UNKNOWN and block the currency and tax backfill design.
The restricted security annex items of the E09 audit (SEC-E09-xx) were not read; the way the delivery-country check differs between checkout paths is described only as a design gap, without detail.

The plan sentence on visitors from a non-active country is line 191 of the plan file while the unit text cites 187-189; lines 187-191 are covered. Line 13 (receiving orders is independent of the country merely existing) is outside the stated ranges but is the basis of the owned sale-refusal rule, so D1-16 cites it.

Not traced: the auction module claim checkout, the admin and vendor POS order writers beyond id generation, the sales-channel webhooks beyond the dispatch materializer, the seller app (only PR 3 and the POS key note were considered) and the customer app order and invoice screens beyond the checkout gate and the currency parameter.

The bodies of #8, #19, #28, #37, #38, #39, #50 and #64 were not read in full (index titles only). Their code was read where it feeds D1: resolver, context, middleware, legal readiness and the storefront list. #37, #50 and #64 were not read beyond their titles.

Gateway refund and webhook logic, wallet debits, coupons and shipping rules were not assessed here (units D2, E, I1 and H1).

cross_axis_notes.text: Payment method eligibility on a route (cards, wallets, cash on delivery by destination country and merchant account) is D2's. The H1-06 engine only calls a hook. Baseline in main: CheckoutCodGuard (mixed-provider cash on delivery) and the per-provider cod_supported and cod_verified settings.
C-16 is to pin that a destination never changes which product row's stock is taken. H1-07 adds the seller, selling-company and order-stamp half. Share the foreign-address fixtures between the two.

One provider per product and country, no automatic fallback, the historical execution source, pools, reservations, safety buffers, the outbox, stock-writer idempotency and concurrency, no second inventory engine, and provider versus sales channel are stock-source topics held by C (C-01 to C-17).

C judged the same carrier lines from the stock side: C-10 (adapters, preflight) MERGED, C-12 (room for other countries) IN PROGRESS, C-15 (Saudi defaults, currency, phone) NOT STARTED, C-18 (Torod and M5AZN) INTEGRATED AND TESTED. H1-11 and H1-12 judge routes and coverage; build the fake third adapter (C-12) and the country defaults (C-15) once.
A2-12 (address eligibility per storefront, NOT STARTED) needs the destination list of H1-01 and the carrier serviceability of H1-05. Implement the list once here and let A2-12 consume it.

Orders keep a snapshot of company, currency, tax, prices, address and execution source. H1 needs the destination country, the shipping quote and the tax and duty lines inside that snapshot (H1-06, H1-07, H1-09). Orders carry no country or currency today.

The SAR default and two-decimal assumptions of config/fulfillment.php and the storefront currency seam (GCC-05) decide the unit of every shipping quote and provider amount (H1-08). The provider side is C-15; the store side belongs to the pricing unit.

Shipping method, zone and rate screens, the Integration Center and provider shipments are in no staff country scope slice (GCC-14c slices 4 to 6 are not built; Discovery E11-F16). H1-14 depends on it.

A 'shipping' document is one of the six legal documents each storefront must publish (config gcc.storefronts.legal.required_documents). Cross-border terms, duty responsibility and returns abroad belong in it; the text is the legal unit's.

cross_axis_notes.text: Axis J also lists the legal documents and their versions (GCC-11 readiness, acceptance receipts, per-country required locales in config/gcc.php). I1 records only the audit of the communication channels (I1-18); legal text, versions and acceptance belong to I2.

The per-store pause (browse-only, maintenance page, redirect; GCC-12, Discovery Q-40) belongs to I2. I1-07 only requires that necessary notifications and the obligations of placed orders keep running while a store pauses.

Recording marketing consent per storefront, legal entity and channel (A2-13, not started) belongs to A2. I1-08 is the sender side: every marketing send consults the record and carries an unsubscribe link.

Carrying the storefront through queue payloads, jobs, CLI and notifications (A1-14, A1-17) belongs to A1. I1-06 depends on a listener running inside the order's storefront; I1-05 and A1-17 both list the topic naming rule as an open owner decision.

Display of coupons, deals, banners and campaigns per store (coupon list and applicable_list narrowing, the experience-campaign cache key per storefront; B-16) belongs to B. I1-12 to I1-15 own the coupon and campaign rules; B-16 owns what the customer sees.

Each storefront's own currency and local pricing without automatic FX (GCC-05) is checkout and pricing work. Coupon amounts in a store's unit (I1-12) can only be built on that seam, which is on a branch without a PR (gcc/p1-storefront-currency, with orders.storefront_country as slice 2).
Brand name, logo and URL per country (GCC-10) are the source of the identity a notification template must render (I1-03); the theme and brand unit owns them.

Staff country scopes for the coupon, campaign, notification, cart-marketing and e-mail-template screens: no rule references them and GCC-14c slice 4 (promotions and storefront content) is not started, so a country-restricted employee holding the marketing permission can still act on every store.

The app side of topics (subscribe and unsubscribe on a storefront change, token update) and in-app push handling belong to the customer app unit; the customer app subscribes to sixvalley, maintenance and theme-update topics and never unsubscribes.
The seller app subscribes to lavkoo_seller, which no backend code sends to (Discovery Q-44); seller topics and seller notifications belong to the seller app unit.
GCC-20 requires admin alert topics never to reuse customer, marketing or seller topics. I1-05 keeps the marketing namespace apart, but the alerts and their topics belong to the Super Admin unit.
hreflang, canonical URLs and the sitemap per language and per market (B-17) belong to B; I1-16 supplies the per-market language list they need.
Behaviour of a country or language change in the apps and the theme caches (plan axis H) belongs to the app and theme units; customer app PR 7 already clears caches on both changes.

tests/Feature/Coupon and tests/Feature/Referral are in no MySQL 8 or MariaDB 11.4.2 group of ci.yml (the groups name Fulfillment + security, Address, Storefront, Catalog, Staff scope, sales channels, concurrency, myfatoorah, costs, strict mode), so PR 2, 4, 5 and 55 run on SQLite only. Adding them to a group is CI work.

coverage_gaps: Nothing was run and no job log was opened: states rest on reading the trees at the stated refs and on job names and conclusions in ci-table.md and ci/*.json. Test counts come from reading test files and PR bodies. The overlay job is not counted as a test failure.

No combined tree of the security set (PR 75) and the GCC chain (PR 83) exists, so no requirement is above IMPLEMENTED IN DRAFT; PR 2, 4 and 5 are in neither tree (their heads are green on their own, SQLite only for the Coupon tests), and PR 55 is in the PR 75 tree only.

Production was not inspected: the live language list and codes (the apps map Arabic to 'sy'), the notification_messages, email_templates and translations rows, the mail, SMS, Zender, Chatwoot and Firebase accounts, the queue driver and the schedule are UNVERIFIED.

Two newer branches without a PR were read only where cited and are not counted: gcc/p1-storefront-currency (GCC-05 slices 1 to 3, orders.storefront_country) and gcc/release/security-gcc-integration-ci (the combined tree); their CI was not read.

Arabic wording was not judged. The locale coverage numbers (en 17,818 keys; sa 11,970 and ks 11,985 at about 95% Arabic; ae 17,726 at about 15%) come from a line-based parse of resources/lang at origin/main and are approximate.

Seller app, delivery-man app and Auction module notification code were read only through constants, PR bodies and the Discovery audit (the delivery-man app is not in the three repositories); the apps were not run, and the customer app's tests were read from the workflow file of PR 7's head.

Legal opt-in rules per country and the privacy retention of delivery logs cannot be assessed from code; the customer-facing consent texts and the necessary-versus-marketing line need legal and native review.

cross_axis_notes.text: SEO, canonical URLs and the old web URLs are web-storefront work (routes, sitemap, redirects). The app owns only App Links and Deep Links (J-16).

Per-country theme, shared component library and brand tokens, drafts, versions, independent publish per store and platform, preview, scheduled publish, rollback, and the backend classes ThemeManager, ThemeBuilderService, ThemeDelivery, StorefrontThemeRenderer, ThemeVersion, ThemeSection, ViewerContext. The app consumes the result (J-05) and adds no theme editor.
GCC-09 also asks for the seller app's theme and API impact to be audited; the customer app side is J-05.

Orders separate per store and selling company, with the company, currency, tax, price, address and fulfillment snapshot, are backend order work (lavkoo#87 slice 2 records storefront and currency on new orders). The app only shows them (J-12).

Wallets separate per store, company and currency are backend ledgers. The app's wallet controller loads when its screen opens and formats with the display currency (J-06); a browse-only storefront refuses top-ups (J-08).
A local manager must not see another country's customer transactions: admin authorization and queries, not the app.

Shared or separate e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp and push profiles per store, shared templates with country and language overrides, idempotency and delivery logs, and the existing PushNotificationTrait, NotificationController and EmailTemplates are backend. The app side is J-11.

Tabby and Tamara review, gateway eligibility per market, method, currency and merchant, accounts and secrets per legal entity, webhook verification, refunds and reconciliation are backend. The app starts payments and reads results (J-10).
One store and one selling company per checkout, local prices, no auto-FX and the order snapshot are backend pricing and order rules. The app's display part is J-06 and its cart part is J-07.

Approved legal documents per country, versions, effective dates, PolicyRegistry versus policy pages and the independent legal review are backend and legal work. The app shows pages and records acceptance (J-14).

Preparing a store before activation, the admin states Draft, Ready and Active, the pause settings, and keeping webhooks, refunds, settlements, shipments and support alive while paused are backend. The app side is J-08 and J-09.
Which address a storefront can serve (provider, product restrictions, destination, tax) is shipping and address backend work. The app side is J-13.
Store release of the app, version numbering (pubspec 3.0.6+48 against appVersion 16.2.1) and the live shop floor are deployment matters. The app-side gate is J-17.

coverage_gaps: No Flutter SDK, device or emulator was used (read-only assessment): nothing was built, analysed or run. Every 'green' is the conclusion of a GitHub check run read from ci-table.md and ci/lavkooapp-*.json (job name and conclusion only, no logs). The two render-matrix failures, the 255 analyzer findings and the whole-suite counts come from the bodies of lavkooapp#5 to #7, not from a run.

Native configuration was read as text (AndroidManifest.xml, Runner.entitlements, Info.plist, router); the Android assetlinks and iOS apple-app-site-association files served by the live domain, and the store listings, were not inspected.

field_corrections.field: ac.t of 'A default that is unknown, incomplete or inactive is refused, also while the flag is off'
field_corrections.problem: True only for the bare constructor: StorefrontResolverTest::test_an_inactive_default_country_is_refused_even_while_switched_off builds new StorefrontResolver directly. A request goes through StorefrontResolver::fromConfig() (ResolveStorefront::handle line 21), whose flag-off branch (StorefrontResolver.php lines 52-58) replaces an unknown, inactive or incomplete default by the built-in Saudi storefront instead of refusing it; ResolveStorefrontMiddlewareTest::test_while_switched_off_a_missing_or_broken_configuration_still_serves_saudi pins that for 'an unknown default country', 'an inactive default country' and 'a default country without a currency'. The constructor checks completeness only while enabled, so an incomplete default is not refused while off and no test says it is.
field_corrections.replacement: A default that is unknown or inactive makes the resolver constructor throw in both modes. For a request, an unusable (unknown, inactive or incomplete) default fails the request while storefronts are on; while they are off the built-in Saudi storefront serves instead (the behaviour of A1-01 AC4). MET holds for this wording only.

field_corrections.problem: Credits PR 19 with refusing an unknown, incomplete or inactive default also while off. PR 8 refuses an unknown default and PR 19 an inactive one, both in the constructor only. field_corrections.problem: The sentence 'vendor_app is registered but not renderable' is true only for publishing. Delivery does not refuse vendor_app: ComponentCapabilityRegistry::servableTo/servableToChannel (returns [] for vendor_app) has no caller in as-main, gcc-ci or as-sec (git grep servableTo finds only the definition and its own delegate). Channel::RENDERABLE is read only by AppBuilderController:85, PublishValidator:220 and ExperiencePageService:181. ThemeDelivery::build runs only SectionVisibility::passes and clientHolds, neither of which checks vendor_app. ThemeDelivery::fingerprint (platform, device, audience, segments, locale, engine, schema, components) omits the channel. The legacy /api/v1/theme/sections builds from the web renderer's web ViewerContext (StorefrontThemeRenderer::runnable), so AC 1 holds for /theme/home and the web page only (E07-F14).
field_corrections.replacement: Section-level platforms and channels (web, customer_app, vendor_app) and a page-level channel restrict what each client draws. vendor_app is registered and cannot be published to alone (Channel::RENDERABLE is read only by AppBuilderController:85, PublishValidator:220, ExperiencePageService:181), but delivery does not refuse it: servableTo/servableToChannel (empty for vendor_app) has no caller, and ThemeDelivery::build runs only SectionVisibility::passes and clientHolds, so a request with X-UI-Channel: vendor_app (or ?channel=) to /api/v1/theme/home is served every section whose channels column is empty. The delivery cache fingerprint has no channel, so payloads built for different channels can share an entry. The legacy /api/v1/theme/sections uses the web ViewerContext: a web-only section is present and a customer_app-only section absent for every caller. The seller app calls no theme API on any of its 7 refs and reads only config active_theme (theme_root_path() always returns 'default'). One version, one publish and one token set serve both channels.
